headline: Meta reportedly developing camera-free smart glasses for October launch
summary: Meta is reportedly developing new smart glasses, codenamed Luna, without a camera, aiming to ship as early as October to address privacy concerns and attract new customers.
details: Meta is reportedly developing a new pair of smart glasses, codenamed Luna, that will ship without a camera as early as October. The company may unveil the new model at its Connect developer conference on September 23-24, with two styles: Clubmaster and Burbank.

While lacking a camera, Luna will feature six built-in microphones and speakers directed towards the user's ears. This setup is designed to facilitate interaction with Meta's AI chatbot, making the glasses functional for voice commands and audio output.

The removal of the camera aims to counter privacy concerns that have plagued Meta's current smart glasses, which critics have labeled "pervert glasses." Despite previous updates to prevent tampering with recording indicator LEDs, the existing models have garnered a negative reputation.
By offering a camera-less option, Meta hopes to attract hesitant potential customers. The new Luna glasses will also feature slimmer temples, designed to make them appear more like ordinary eyewear.

headline_marked: [[Rome: The Agentic OS That Compounds]] – a new approach for self-improving AI agents
headline: Rome: The Agentic OS That Compounds – a new approach for self-improving AI agents
summary: This early-stage open-source project aims to build an operating system where AI agents can accumulate memory, refine capabilities, and self-improve over time, unlike current one-shot tools.
details: Most AI assistants today operate as one-shot tools, completing a task without retaining memory or gaining capabilities. Rome, an open-source project with 502 stars, introduces an "agentic OS" designed for humans and agents.

Rome aims to create an environment where recursive agents can accumulate knowledge, refine their processes, and self-improve as they run. This differs from simple model wrappers by providing a substrate with state, memory, interoperability, and self-evolution.

Described as an attempt at "the operating system of the agent era," Rome is built as lower-level engineering using a TypeScript monorepo. It includes both frontend and backend components, targeting developers interested in agent architecture.

The project is in its very early stages, with 502 stars and 41 forks, and is rapidly evolving. It is not intended as a mature, drop-in replacement for existing toolchains but rather as a foundation for studying and building agent substrates.
